thread:
maria: Heads-up — saw a 15% TP tail latency regression on the latest canary. Perf traces point to all-reduce stalls for small tensor chunks.
chris: Can you paste the perf summary? Is this ring vs tree related or something else like kernel packing?
maria: Dump from perf-bot attached below. Short version: when microbatching target=8 we get ~256KB allreduce msgs -> ring latency climbs, and comm/compute overlap drops. When we increase microbatch to 12 msgs jump to ~600KB and latency per allreduce drops.
sam: Sounds like message size is crossing a sweet spot for ring. Tree favors small messages. Any NCCL knobs enabled?
maria: We run default NCCL config. Perf-bot suggests switching to tree for shard sizes <512k. Perf logs:
```
[perf-bot] summary: step=240, tp=2, microbatch=8
allreduce_chunks=32, avg_msg=270KB, ring_latency=1.8ms, tree_latency=1.1ms
overlap_ratio=0.42, compute_wait=0.9ms
```
lee: Interesting — KV cache is shaving sequences earlier which reduces token aggregation across ranks -> smaller reduce messages.
toni: So the runtime's batching heuristic + kvcache eviction is indirectly changing allreduce msgsize. We should consider promoting chunk coalescing before NCCL call.
chris: Agreed. Options:
- enable NCCL tree for small msg sizes (NCCL_ALGO=Tree / NCCL_TOPO=auto)
- adjust chunk_size to align with 512KB boundary
- change microbatch schedule to favor slightly larger microbatches
- add local coalesce pass in runtime before allreduce
maria: Quick repro script I used:
```
export NCCL_ALGO=Ring
./run_infer --tp 2 --microbatch 8 --kvpub false --profile /tmp/pf.json
redwood-prof --collect nccl --file /tmp/pf.json | jq .allreduce
```
perf-bot: Collected nccl timeline: ring stalls spike at chunk boundaries, 80% of stalls flagged as send/recv queue contention. Trace id: pf-1999.
sam: Can we try a tree fallback in runtime when avg_msg < 512KB? Could be a cheap heuristic.
lee: Also test chunk coalescing: coalesce smaller KV updates within the same step into bigger tensors before allreduce. That should improve ring perf.
toni: Be careful — coalescing increases GPU memory spike. Add a memory guard threshold.
maria: I'll run two runs this afternoon: (1) runtime tree-fallback for small msgs, (2) coalescing with memory guard. Posting results here.
chris: If the tree fallback helps, we should add an automatic policy in the kernel-selector: prefer tree for small message sizes and ring for >1MB.
maria: Noted. Also checking whether kernel selection (attention QKV kernel) is interacting — smaller msg sizes produce more fragmented kernels and more frequent kernel launches, which further hurts overlap.
sam: Can you capture nvprof/ncu for the next run so we see kernel launch frequency? Even a small reduction in launch count can improve overlap.
maria: Yep. Scheduling run now. ETA ~3h. Will drop the trace and perf-bot summary when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Reminder: `redwood-prof` supports --compare to baseline which saves time when triaging regressions.
chris: Great. If this reproduces, open a tiny RFC for the selector change + unit-test on perf harness.
maria: Will do.
